title: SBI Liveness Profile 0.1 (proposal)
description: Optional, backward-compatible additions to the MOSIP Secure Biometric Interface for face devices. Requests follow the SBI convention that every scalar is a JSON string; responses and signed data may use booleans and arrays where the SBI does. The $id is a placeholder until the specification has a home (Bible Part 30, Q12).

TransactionId.description: SBI transactionId: letters, digits and hyphens only. PRAMAAN uses 32 lower-case hex characters.

Hex32.description: 32 bytes in lower-case hex: an HMAC-SHA256 tag or a SHA-256 hash.

DeviceInfoLivenessProfile.description: The livenessProfile object added to the device-info response (point 1).

signedStream.description: The device authenticates each preview frame (point 2).

illuminatorControl.description: Illuminators the client may drive with illuminate (point 5). Empty if none.

sensorTimestamps.description: Frame times come from the sensor, not the host.

KeyAgreementRequest.description: Sent with the stream-start request (point 2). The client's ephemeral P-256 key, X.509 SubjectPublicKeyInfo, standard base64.

KeyAgreementAnswer.description: The payload of the compact JWS (RS256, device certificate chain in x5c) with which the device answers. clientEphemeralKeyHash is the SHA-256 of the client key it answered, so a swapped client key is detected.

StreamCheckpoint.description: The payload of the compact JWS the device emits every N frames: '<frame index>:<tag hex>'. Frame 0 is tag_0.

CaptureExtras.description: Fields the device adds inside the signed capture data (points 3 and 6).

CaptureBurstRequest.description: captureBurst (point 4): several signed frames during a challenge. Every scalar is a string.

IlluminateRequest.description: illuminate (point 5): the client's random schedule. Colour changes must obey the photosensitivity limits in the specification (at most 3 per second, steps of at least 333 ms). Every scalar is a string.

EmissionLog.description: The payload of the compact JWS with which the device reports what its illuminator actually did. atMs is relative to the first emission.
